messages.body_plain:
Just saw the messages. Somehow messages are not coming to the same thread
in which I posted !.

Michael, can you please point to the file which has this code in your
codebase ?



Thanks,
Srikanth.

On Tue, Sep 27, 2016 at 2:00 PM, <
stats-rosuda-devel-request at listserv.uni-augsburg.de> wrote:

> Send stats-rosuda-devel mailing list submissions to

>
> or, via email, send a message with subject or body 'help' to
>         stats-rosuda-devel-request at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
>
> You can reach the person managing the list at
>         stats-rosuda-devel-owner at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
>
> When replying, please edit your Subject line so it is more specific
> than "Re: Contents of stats-rosuda-devel digest..."
>
>
> Today's Topics:
>
>    1. Re: Getting R plots back to the Client (Michael C Rosenstein)
>    2. Re: Getting R plots back to the Client (Simon Urbanek)
>
>
> ----------------------------------------------------------------------
>
> Message: 1
> Date: Mon, 26 Sep 2016 08:15:05 -0400
> From: Michael C Rosenstein <mcr at mdibl.org>
> To: stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
> Subject: Re: [stats-rosuda-devel] Getting R plots back to the Client
> Message-ID: <5e11cb7c-30a5-589f-849c-691158f8d6c6 at mdibl.org>
> Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8; format=flowed
>
> > I'm using RServe through Java client. Basically I'll send a file to my R
> > package's function and the function returns back the plot. Any
> > ideas/existing snippets on retrieving the plot ?
>
> This is a simplified version of what we do:
>
> final RFileInputStream remoteFileStream = conn.openFile(remoteFilePath);
> final byte[] fileBytes = IOUtils.toByteArray(remoteFileStream);
> conn.removeFile(remoteFilePath);
> return fileBytes;
>
>
>
>
>
>
> ------------------------------
>
> Message: 2
> Date: Mon, 26 Sep 2016 09:08:13 -0400
> From: Simon Urbanek <simon.urbanek at r-project.org>
> To: Michael C Rosenstein <mcr at mdibl.org>
> Cc: "Apple Inc." <stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de>
> Subject: Re: [stats-rosuda-devel] Getting R plots back to the Client
> Message-ID: <6929F80E-2411-4461-8A84-F7BBADF6AE47 at r-project.org>
> Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
>
> Note that even without enabled I/O you can use something like
>
> byte x[] = c.eval("readBin('filename',raw(),file.info('filename')$
> size)").asBytes();
>
> The difference between using I/O and the above is that the above results
> in one message whereas I/O uses multiple messages to send the payload in
> chunks (i.e., has lower memory footprint for large files).
>
> Cheers,
> Simon
>
>
>
> > On Sep 26, 2016, at 8:15 AM, Michael C Rosenstein <mcr at mdibl.org> wrote:
> >
> >> I'm using RServe through Java client. Basically I'll send a file to my R
> >> package's function and the function returns back the plot. Any
> >> ideas/existing snippets on retrieving the plot ?
> >
> > This is a simplified version of what we do:

> > final RFileInputStream remoteFileStream = conn.openFile(remoteFilePath);
> > final byte[] fileBytes = IOUtils.toByteArray(remoteFileStream);
> > conn.removeFile(remoteFilePath);
> > return fileBytes;
> >
